question.worked_solution:
First, we find the first-order derivative ${f}_{z}(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{z}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\frac{z}{x+z}) \\  & =\frac{x}{(x+z)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find ${f}_{zx}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating ${f}_{z}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{zx}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{z}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{x}{(x+z)^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{(x+z)^{2}-2x(x+z)}{(x+z)^{4}} \\  & =\frac{z-x}{(x+z)^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${f}_{zxx}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating ${f}_{zx}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{zxx}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{zy}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{z-x}{(x+z)^{3}}) \\  & =\frac{-(x+z)^{3}-3(z-x)(x+z)^{2}}{(x+z)^{6}} \\  & =\frac{2(x-2z)}{(x+z)^{4}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we evaluate ${f}_{zxx}(x,y,z)$ at $(1,0,1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{zxx}(1,0,1) & =\frac{2(1-2(1))}{(1+1)^{4}}=\frac{-2}{16}=-\frac{1}{8}\end{aligned}
$$
